title: feat(plugin-auth,platform-objects,core)!: a key a forced password reset revoked is restored by a platform administrator only
body:
Fixes #23993

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

An API key that an administrator's forced password reset revoked can now be restored only by a platform administrator. Its owner is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, and the refusal names both roads: ask a platform administrator, or create a new key. This follows the changeset of #23287 ruling C′ (`.changeset/pre/23287-api-key-account-posture.md`): "an administrator can restore a key a routine reset revoked …, or the owner mints a replacement". The field widens `sys_api_key`; the owner's restore of such a key narrows.

## What changed

| file | change |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts` | `revoked_reason`: a readonly `select` (ADR-0092 D4) whose one option is `admin_password_reset`, described for an administrator |
| `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/*.objects.generated.ts` | `en` regenerated (`pnpm i18n:extract`); the `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` leaves are hand-written, and the re-run extract kept them and dropped their source-fill hashes |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revocation.ts` | the stamp: `revoked_reason: admin_password_reset` is written beside `revoked: true`. This is the only place the reason is set. A key already revoked before the reset is not written, so it keeps no reason |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.ts` (new) | ONE `beforeUpdate` hook on `sys_api_key`, at priority 15, after the ADR-0092 D2 guard (10). It enforces the rules listed below |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` | only the hook's registration in `kernel:ready`, beside `registerIdentityWriteGuard` |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/managed-extension-fields.ts` | `revoked_reason` added to `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS.sys_api_key`, and NOT to the editable map |
| `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts` | only the `API_KEY_REVOKED` message, which now branches on `row.revoked_reason`. Code, status, order and carried fields are unchanged |
| `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` | only `API_KEY_REVOKED` |
| `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` | **one row (26b), outside the claimed surface.** See Deviation below |
| `.changeset/23993-reset-revoked-key-restore.md` | `minor` for `platform-objects`, `plugin-auth` and `core`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` |

The hook's rules:

1. A user-context un-revoke (any `revoked` value that is not true) is refused when the row's stored `revoked_reason` is `admin_password_reset` (or no pre-image is in hand), unless the caller passes `hasPlatformAdminStanding(engine, session.userId)`. That is the ADR-0068 D2 PLATFORM_ADMIN rung, and it fails closed.
2. Every un-revoke the hook admits clears `revoked_reason`, including an administrator's.
3. A revoke, or a write that leaves `revoked` alone, never touches the reason. So `{ revoked: true }` on an already-revoked key keeps it. A caller-sent `revoked_reason` is withheld by the engine's readonly strip and by D2, so it cannot clear the reason either.
4. A system-context write is never refused: the mint, the `last_used_at` stamp and the forced reset all pass.

## Measured before building

Both measurements used a throwaway probe on a real `ObjectQL` engine over SQLite, a `beforeUpdate` hook at priority 15, and a user context. The probe was deleted and never committed.

- **A hook's write of a `readonly` column on a user-context update persists.**
  - By id, the hook writing `'a'` persisted `'a'`.
  - When the caller forged a value and the hook wrote `null`, `null` persisted; the forgery was not handed back.
- **A multi-row update judges each row by its own pre-image.**
  - Two rows stored `b` and `a`; the per-row `previous` the hook saw was `r1=b`, `r2=a`.
  - The hook's in-place `null` landed on both rows.

Neither reading falsifies the hook route.

## Pins and their red legs

All pins run on the real write path: real `ObjectQL` over SQLite, the real `SecurityPlugin` with the shipped permission sets (the owner resolves `member_default` and its `sys_api_key_self` row scope; the administrator holds the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant that `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` writes), the D2 guard with the whitelists `auth-plugin.ts` registers, the real forced-reset revocation and the real key door.

Each red leg was made with `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode against the committed fix (`39730a73e`): the anchor hit 1 → 0, the blob changed, and the restore was proven blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty. An outer trap restored from `HEAD` by absolute path. The CONTROL stayed green on every leg.

| # | pin (file) | green | red leg |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the owner's restore of a reset-revoked key is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, the message names the platform administrator and `POST /api/v1/keys`, and the row is unchanged (`api-key-restore-guard.test.ts`) | ✓ | L1, drop `throw restoreRefused()`: red |
| 2 | a platform-admin restore lands, the reason clears, and the key door admits the key (same file) | ✓ | L2, drop the clear: red |
| 3 | CONTROL: the owner revokes and restores a plain key, and no reason is ever recorded (same file) | ✓ | green on every leg |
| 4 | the owner re-revoking a reset-revoked key keeps the reason, a forged `revoked_reason: null` is withheld, and the restore after it is still refused (same file) | ✓ | L1: red |
| 5 | the forced reset stamps `admin_password_reset`, and a key revoked before it keeps no reason (same file, and the `DEFAULT ON` case of `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts`) | ✓ | L3, drop the stamp: red in both files |
| 6 | the message names the restorer per reason (`core` `api-key-lifecycle.test.ts`; end to end through the key door in `api-key-restore-guard.test.ts`) | ✓ | L4, message branch forced to `false`: red |
| + | multi-row: an owner batch that includes a reset-revoked key is refused whole and neither row moves; an owner batch of plain keys is admitted; an administrator batch clears the reason on every row | ✓ | L1: owner batch red; L2: administrator batch red |
| + | system context: an un-revoke lands and clears the reason, and a `last_used_at` stamp leaves it | ✓ | L2: red |
| + | `auth-plugin.ts` registers exactly one `beforeUpdate` hook on `sys_api_key` at a priority after the D2 guard | ✓ | L5, registration removed: red |

Red-leg counts: L1 3 failed of 11; L2 3 of 11; L3 7 of 68 (the two files together); L4 1 of 22; L5 1 of 11 (that run used `-t kernel:ready`, so 10 were skipped).

## Tests

- `plugin-auth`, full suite, two shards (`vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --shard=1/2` and `2/2`): 76 + 75 files, 1753 + 1202 tests passed (10 skipped). Lock verdicts were command-exit 0.
- `platform-objects`, full suite: 73 files, 1136 tests passed.
- `core`: `api-key-lifecycle`, `api-key` and `api-key-account-posture` tests, 61 passed.
- Typecheck of `core`, `platform-objects` and `plugin-auth`: exit 0, with `check:test-typecheck` OK on each. The `plugin-auth` ledger is unchanged at 10 files / 88 errors / 23 signatures.
- Re-run on the merged head `17ca3f000` (after `origin/main` up to `2b274600b`): the plugin-auth pins and neighbouring suites (125 tests), `core` api-key (61) and `platform-objects` sys_api_key and translations (144) all passed.
- `test:repo` was not run locally; it is CI's.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derived 102 commands at the final head `f782520bf`. Every command was run with its exit captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: **102 derived, 102 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, and every command exited 0. That includes `check:auth-mount-ledger`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-stale-fill`, `check:system-context-census`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check:empty-changeset`.

The artifact-roster block marks four families whose roster sits under one of these paths: `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing` and `check:filter-alias-parity`. The wide-population block declares ten: `init-service-contract`, `live-db-isolation`, `meta-type-normalized`, `optional-error-sink`, `resume-authority-declared`, `runner-env-posture`, `settings-bind-window`, `startup-registry-verdict`, `verify-stand-in` and `wildcard-fallthrough`. All fourteen were also run locally, and each exited 0. CI's check-runs are the verdict for the rest.

## Deviation: one row outside the amended surface

`check:system-context-census` failed on the new hook: `[file-without-a-row] … api-key-restore-guard.ts holds 1 elevation read site(s) … (isUserContextWrite)`. The hook must read `isSystem` (rule 4), and that page holds every such read site. So the page gains row 26b, anchored `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.ts#isUserContextWrite`. Without it the required `Lint & Repo Gates` goes red. This page is not in the claim's surface and needs the seat's declaration (`domain:devx`, as `error-catalog.mdx` was).

## Acceptance notes

- **Rows revoked before this lands.** Keys a forced reset revoked before this change carry no reason and stay owner-restorable. That population exists only on `@objectstack/plugin-auth@18.0.0-next.2` (dist-tag `next`) and on `main` builds since 2026-10-14. There is no backfill: the reset's audit row records counts, not key ids.
- **A key the owner revoked before a forced reset.** The reset revokes only keys that are not yet revoked, so such a key gets no reason, and its owner can restore it afterwards. This keeps the reason truthful (the reset did not revoke that key). Whether the reset should also stamp keys that were already revoked is not decided here.
- **A duplicated predicate.** The hook's user-context predicate repeats the D2 guard's one line (`identity-write-guard.ts`, module-private and outside the surface). The two judge the same writes.
- **No UI courtesy.** The Restore API Key action still renders for the owner on a reset-revoked key, and the server refuses it with the road. A `visible` predicate on the action would be a follow-up.
